import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.3

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and $p$ a prime. Let $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ be the
group of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers modulo $p^m$ such that
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. The group
$P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is a finite $p$-group. For which $m$ and $n$ is it regular?

Here both congruences are modulo $p$: $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is the group of matrices over
$\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ whose reduction modulo $p$ is upper unitriangular, i.e. a Sylow $p$-subgroup
of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. (Requiring $a_{ii} = 1$ exactly in $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ would not give
a group when $m, n \geq 2$.)

A finite $p$-group $G$ is *regular* (P. Hall) if for all $a, b \in G$ there is
$c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ with $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$, where $\langle a, b \rangle'$
is the derived subgroup of $\langle a, b \rangle$ and $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$.

Editors' comment (2001): The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is known to be regular if $mn < p$
(Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika*, **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59 (Russian)). The case $m = 1$
is completely done by A. V. Yagzhev in (*Math. Notes*, **56**, no. 5–6 (1995), 1283–1290),
although this paper is erroneous for $m > 1$. The case $m = 2$ is completed in
(S. G. Kolesnikov, *Issledovaniya in analysis and algebra*, no. 3, Tomsk Univ., Tomsk, 2001,
117–125 (Russian)).

Editors' comment (2009): The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ was shown to be regular for any $m$
if $n^2 < p$ (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.*, **47**, no. 6 (2006), 1054–1059).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«8.3»
section RegularPGroup
variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

blocks.code:
def agemo (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure ((· ^ p) '' (H : Set G))
blocks.docstring:
The subgroup $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$ of $G$ generated by the $p$-th
powers of the elements of a subgroup $H$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (grepped for agemo/omega subgroup/p-th power subgroup); only Subgroup.closure and commutatorSet exist.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.3».agemo
justification.why_needed: The subgroup ℧₁(H) = ⟨h^p : h ∈ H⟩ generated by p-th powers of a subgroup, needed in Hall's definition of regularity. Defined as Subgroup.closure ((· ^ p) '' H).

blocks.name: agemo
blocks.text:
/-- The subgroup $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$ of $G$ generated by the $p$-th
powers of the elements of a subgroup $H$. -/
def agemo (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure ((· ^ p) '' (H : Set G))

blocks.code:
def IsRegularPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsPGroup p G ∧ ∀ a b : G,
    ∃ c ∈ agemo p ⁅Subgroup.closure {a, b}, Subgroup.closure {a, b}⁆,
      (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p * c
blocks.docstring:
A group $G$ is a *regular $p$-group* in the sense of P. Hall if it is a $p$-group and for
all $a, b \in G$ there is $c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ such that $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$,
where $\langle a, b \rangle'$ is the derived subgroup of the subgroup generated by $a$ and $b$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsPGroup (Mathlib) gives only the p-group part; Subgroup.commutator ⁅H,H⁆ gives the derived subgroup; no regularity predicate exists anywhere (grepped for 'regular p-group', 'IsRegularPGroup', 'Hall.*regular').
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.3».IsRegularPGroup
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a regular p-group in P. Hall's sense. Defined as IsPGroup p G ∧ ∀ a b, ∃ c ∈ agemo p ⁅closure {a,b}, closure {a,b}⁆, (a*b)^p = a^p * b^p * c.

blocks.name: IsRegularPGroup
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is a *regular $p$-group* in the sense of P. Hall if it is a $p$-group and for
all $a, b \in G$ there is $c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ such that $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$,
where $\langle a, b \rangle'$ is the derived subgroup of the subgroup generated by $a$ and $b$. -/
def IsRegularPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsPGroup p G ∧ ∀ a b : G,
    ∃ c ∈ agemo p ⁅Subgroup.closure {a, b}, Subgroup.closure {a, b}⁆,
      (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p * c

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPGroup.isRegularPGroup_of_isMulCommutative {p : ℕ} [IsMulCommutative G]
    (hG : IsPGroup p G) : IsRegularPGroup p G :=
  ⟨hG, fun a b => ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, by rw [(Commute.all a b).mul_pow, mul_one]⟩⟩
blocks.docstring: Every abelian $p$-group is regular: one can take $c = 1$.
blocks.name: IsPGroup.isRegularPGroup_of_isMulCommutative
blocks.text:
/-- Every abelian $p$-group is regular: one can take $c = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPGroup.isRegularPGroup_of_isMulCommutative {p : ℕ} [IsMulCommutative G]
    (hG : IsPGroup p G) : IsRegularPGroup p G :=
  ⟨hG, fun a b => ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, by rw [(Commute.all a b).mul_pow, mul_one]⟩⟩
end RegularPGroup
section MatrixGroup
variable {n p m : ℕ}

blocks.code:
def IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i i - 1) ∧ ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i j
blocks.docstring:
A matrix $(a_{ij})$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ is *unitriangular modulo $p$* if $a_{ii} \equiv 1$
for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matrix.BlockTriangular (Mathlib) only expresses triangularity over the ring itself, not a congruence condition mod p, and has no unit-diagonal variant; no unitriangular group exists in Mathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.3».IsUnitriangularModP
justification.why_needed: Predicate on n×n matrices over ZMod (p^m): a_ii ≡ 1 (mod p) for all i and a_ij ≡ 0 (mod p) for all i > j, written as (p : ZMod (p^m)) ∣ A i i - 1 and (p : ZMod (p^m)) ∣ A i j for j < i. Used as the carrier condition of P and to prove closure lemmas.

blocks.name: IsUnitriangularModP
blocks.text:
/-- A matrix $(a_{ij})$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ is *unitriangular modulo $p$* if $a_{ii} \equiv 1$
for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. -/
def IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i i - 1) ∧ ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i j

blocks.code:
private lemma isUnitriangularModP_iff (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    IsUnitriangularModP A ↔ ∀ i j, j ≤ i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A - 1) i j := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hd, hl⟩ i j hij
    rcases hij.lt_or_eq with h | h
    · simpa [Matrix.one_apply, h.ne'] using hl i j h
    · subst h
      simpa using hd _
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun i => by simpa using h i i le_rfl, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
    simpa [Matrix.one_apply, hij.ne'] using h i j hij.le
blocks.name: isUnitriangularModP_iff

    · simpa [Matrix.one_apply, h.ne'] using hl i j h
    · subst h

blocks.code:
private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.one :
    IsUnitriangularModP (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff]
  simp
blocks.name: IsUnitriangularModP.one
blocks.text:
private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.one :
    IsUnitriangularModP (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff]
  simp

blocks.code:
private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.mul {A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (hB : IsUnitriangularModP B) :
    IsUnitriangularModP (A * B) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff] at hA hB ⊢
  intro i j hij
  have : A * B - 1 = (A - 1) + (B - 1) + (A - 1) * (B - 1) := by noncomm_ring
  rw [this, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
  refine dvd_add (dvd_add (hA i j hij) (hB i j hij)) (Finset.dvd_sum fun k _ => ?_)
  by_cases hk : k ≤ i
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_left (hA i k hk) _
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (hB k j (hij.trans (not_le.mp hk).le)) _
blocks.name: IsUnitriangularModP.mul
blocks.text:
private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.mul {A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (hB : IsUnitriangularModP B) :
    IsUnitriangularModP (A * B) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff] at hA hB ⊢
  intro i j hij
  have : A * B - 1 = (A - 1) + (B - 1) + (A - 1) * (B - 1) := by noncomm_ring
  rw [this, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
  refine dvd_add (dvd_add (hA i j hij) (hB i j hij)) (Finset.dvd_sum fun k _ => ?_)
  by_cases hk : k ≤ i
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_left (hA i k hk) _
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (hB k j (hij.trans (not_le.mp hk).le)) _

blocks.code:
private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.pow {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (k : ℕ) : IsUnitriangularModP (A ^ k) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => exact IsUnitriangularModP.one
  | succ k ih => exact pow_succ A k ▸ ih.mul hA
blocks.name: IsUnitriangularModP.pow
blocks.text:
private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.pow {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (k : ℕ) : IsUnitriangularModP (A ^ k) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => exact IsUnitriangularModP.one
  | succ k ih => exact pow_succ A k ▸ ih.mul hA

blocks.code:
def P [Fact p.Prime] : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) where
  carrier := {A | IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m)))}
  one_mem' := IsUnitriangularModP.one
  mul_mem' hA hB := hA.mul hB
  inv_mem' {A} hA := by
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := (isOfFinOrder_of_finite A).mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers.mpr
      (Subgroup.inv_mem _ (Subgroup.mem_zpowers A))
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ← hk]
    exact hA.pow k
blocks.docstring:
The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers
modulo $p^m$ such that $a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all
$i > j$, as a subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. Every such matrix is invertible, since its
determinant is $\equiv 1 \pmod p$ and hence a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$, so nothing is lost by
working inside $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup and Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Mathlib) — no congruence/Sylow/unitriangular subgroups are available.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.3».P
justification.why_needed: The group P_n(Z_{p^m}) of the problem, as a Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) with carrier the matrices that are unitriangular mod p. one_mem'/mul_mem' are proved directly; inv_mem' uses finiteness of GL over the finite ring (A⁻¹ is a positive power of A), which is why the definition carries [Fact p.Prime].

blocks.name: P
blocks.text:
variable (n p m) in
/-- The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers
modulo $p^m$ such that $a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all
$i > j$, as a subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. Every such matrix is invertible, since its
determinant is $\equiv 1 \pmod p$ and hence a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$, so nothing is lost by
working inside $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. -/
def P [Fact p.Prime] : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) where
  carrier := {A | IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m)))}
  one_mem' := IsUnitriangularModP.one
  mul_mem' hA hB := hA.mul hB
  inv_mem' {A} hA := by
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := (isOfFinOrder_of_finite A).mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers.mpr
      (Subgroup.inv_mem _ (Subgroup.mem_zpowers A))
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ← hk]
    exact hA.pow k

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_P_iff [Fact p.Prime] (A : GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    A ∈ P n p m ↔
      (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i i - 1) ∧
        ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i j :=
  Iff.rfl
blocks.docstring:
Membership in `P n p m` unfolds to the defining congruences: `A ∈ P n p m` if and only if
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_P_iff [Fact p.Prime] (A : GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    A ∈ P n p m ↔
      (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i i - 1) ∧
        ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i j :=

end MatrixGroup

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers and $p$ a prime. Let $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ be the
group of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers modulo $p^m$ such that
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. The group
$P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is a finite $p$-group. For which $m$ and $n$ is it regular?

Here both congruences are modulo $p$: $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is the group of matrices over
$\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ whose reduction modulo $p$ is upper unitriangular, i.e. a Sylow $p$-subgroup
of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. (Requiring $a_{ii} = 1$ exactly in $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ would not give
a group when $m, n \geq 2$.)

A finite $p$-group $G$ is *regular* (P. Hall) if for all $a, b \in G$ there is
$c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ with $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$, where $\langle a, b \rangle'$
is the derived subgroup of $\langle a, b \rangle$ and $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$.

Editors' comment (2001): The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is known to be regular if $mn < p$
(Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika*, **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59 (Russian)). The case $m = 1$
is completely done by A. V. Yagzhev in (*Math. Notes*, **56**, no. 5–6 (1995), 1283–1290),
although this paper is erroneous for $m > 1$. The case $m = 2$ is completed in
(S. G. Kolesnikov, *Issledovaniya in analysis and algebra*, no. 3, Tomsk Univ., Tomsk, 2001,
117–125 (Russian)).

Editors' comment (2009): The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ was shown to be regular for any $m$
if $n^2 < p$ (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.*, **47**, no. 6 (2006), 1054–1059).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.3»

section RegularPGroup

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The subgroup $\mho_1(H) = \langle h^p : h \in H \rangle$ of $G$ generated by the $p$-th
powers of the elements of a subgroup $H$. -/
def agemo (p : ℕ) (H : Subgroup G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure ((· ^ p) '' (H : Set G))

/-- A group $G$ is a *regular $p$-group* in the sense of P. Hall if it is a $p$-group and for
all $a, b \in G$ there is $c \in \mho_1(\langle a, b \rangle')$ such that $(ab)^p = a^p b^p c$,
where $\langle a, b \rangle'$ is the derived subgroup of the subgroup generated by $a$ and $b$. -/
def IsRegularPGroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsPGroup p G ∧ ∀ a b : G,
    ∃ c ∈ agemo p ⁅Subgroup.closure {a, b}, Subgroup.closure {a, b}⁆,
      (a * b) ^ p = a ^ p * b ^ p * c

/-- Every abelian $p$-group is regular: one can take $c = 1$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsPGroup.isRegularPGroup_of_isMulCommutative {p : ℕ} [IsMulCommutative G]
    (hG : IsPGroup p G) : IsRegularPGroup p G :=
  ⟨hG, fun a b => ⟨1, Subgroup.one_mem _, by rw [(Commute.all a b).mul_pow, mul_one]⟩⟩

end RegularPGroup

section MatrixGroup

variable {n p m : ℕ}

/-- A matrix $(a_{ij})$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$ is *unitriangular modulo $p$* if $a_{ii} \equiv 1$
for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. -/
def IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i i - 1) ∧ ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ A i j

private lemma isUnitriangularModP_iff (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    IsUnitriangularModP A ↔ ∀ i j, j ≤ i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A - 1) i j := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hd, hl⟩ i j hij
    rcases hij.lt_or_eq with h | h
    · simpa [Matrix.one_apply, h.ne'] using hl i j h
    · subst h
      simpa using hd _
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun i => by simpa using h i i le_rfl, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
    simpa [Matrix.one_apply, hij.ne'] using h i j hij.le

private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.one :
    IsUnitriangularModP (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff]
  simp

private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.mul {A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (hB : IsUnitriangularModP B) :
    IsUnitriangularModP (A * B) := by
  rw [isUnitriangularModP_iff] at hA hB ⊢
  intro i j hij
  have : A * B - 1 = (A - 1) + (B - 1) + (A - 1) * (B - 1) := by noncomm_ring
  rw [this, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.mul_apply]
  refine dvd_add (dvd_add (hA i j hij) (hB i j hij)) (Finset.dvd_sum fun k _ => ?_)
  by_cases hk : k ≤ i
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_left (hA i k hk) _
  · exact dvd_mul_of_dvd_right (hB k j (hij.trans (not_le.mp hk).le)) _

private lemma IsUnitriangularModP.pow {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))}
    (hA : IsUnitriangularModP A) (k : ℕ) : IsUnitriangularModP (A ^ k) := by
  induction k with
  | zero => exact IsUnitriangularModP.one
  | succ k ih => exact pow_succ A k ▸ ih.mul hA

variable (n p m) in
/-- The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ of all $n \times n$ matrices $(a_{ij})$ over the integers
modulo $p^m$ such that $a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all
$i > j$, as a subgroup of $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. Every such matrix is invertible, since its
determinant is $\equiv 1 \pmod p$ and hence a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/p^m$, so nothing is lost by
working inside $GL_n(\mathbb{Z}/p^m)$. -/
def P [Fact p.Prime] : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) where
  carrier := {A | IsUnitriangularModP (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m)))}
  one_mem' := IsUnitriangularModP.one
  mul_mem' hA hB := hA.mul hB
  inv_mem' {A} hA := by
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := (isOfFinOrder_of_finite A).mem_powers_iff_mem_zpowers.mpr
      (Subgroup.inv_mem _ (Subgroup.mem_zpowers A))
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ← hk]
    exact hA.pow k

/-- Membership in `P n p m` unfolds to the defining congruences: `A ∈ P n p m` if and only if
$a_{ii} \equiv 1$ for all $i$ and $a_{ij} \equiv 0 \pmod p$ for all $i > j$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_P_iff [Fact p.Prime] (A : GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) :
    A ∈ P n p m ↔
      (∀ i, (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i i - 1) ∧
        ∀ i j, j < i → (p : ZMod (p ^ m)) ∣ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod (p ^ m))) i j :=
  Iff.rfl

end MatrixGroup

/-- Let $p$ be a prime and $m, n$ positive integers. The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ is known
to be regular if $mn < p$ (Yu. I. Merzlyakov, *Algebra i Logika*, **3**, no. 4 (1964), 49–59
(Russian)). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.3».variants.merzlyakov_1964 (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (m n : ℕ)
    (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (h : m * n < p) :
    IsRegularPGroup p (P n p m) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $p$ be a prime and $m, n$ positive integers. The group $P_n(\mathbb{Z}_{p^m})$ was shown
to be regular for any $m$ if $n^2 < p$ (S. G. Kolesnikov, *Siberian Math. J.*, **47**, no. 6
(2006), 1054–1059). The bound does not depend on $m$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.3».variants.kolesnikov_2006 (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (m n : ℕ)
    (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (h : n ^ 2 < p) :
    IsRegularPGroup p (P n p m) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.3»

items: Reading of the diagonal condition: the notebook writes 'a_ii ≡ 1 for all i and a_ij ≡ 0 (mod p) for all i > j'. I read BOTH congruences modulo p (P_n is the preimage of the upper unitriangular group under reduction mod p, i.e. a Sylow p-subgroup of GL_n(Z/p^m)). The alternative reading a_ii = 1 exactly in Z/p^m does not define a group when m, n ≥ 2 (e.g. [[1,1],[p,1]]^2 has (1,1)-entry 1+p over Z/p^2), so it cannot be intended. This is noted in the module docstring.
Congruence 'x ≡ 0 (mod p)' for x ∈ ZMod (p^m) is encoded as divisibility (p : ZMod (p^m)) ∣ x, which is equivalent for m ≥ 1 and avoids a side condition m ≠ 0 that ZMod.castHom would need.

IsRegularPGroup p G includes the conjunct IsPGroup p G (so it literally means 'G is a regular p-group'); the source itself asserts P_n(Z_{p^m}) is a finite p-group, so this adds no false claim. Hall's condition is stated with c ∈ ℧₁(⟨a,b⟩') and (ab)^p = a^p b^p c (equivalent to the product-of-p-th-powers form since ℧₁ is generated by p-th powers).

P n p m carries a [Fact p.Prime] instance argument; it is only used to obtain finiteness of GL (Fin n) (ZMod (p^m)) for the proof of inv_mem'. The slot theorems use the same [Fact p.Prime] hypothesis for 'p a prime'.
The positivity hypotheses 0 < m and 0 < n are kept as in the source ('positive integers') although they are mathematically inessential for the truth of the statements.
Two fully proved @[category API] lemmas were added as sanity tests of the bespoke definitions (mem_P_iff unfolding the defining congruences, and abelian p-groups are regular). They are not slots.
AMS tag 20 only (group theory); 15 (matrix theory) could also be argued.

reviewer_notes:
Ambiguity in the source: the diagonal condition is written 'a_ii ≡ 1' with the '(mod p)' only trailing the second congruence. All eight candidates (and I) read both congruences modulo p. This is forced: with a_ii = 1 exactly in Z/p^m the set is not closed under multiplication for m, n ≥ 2 (e.g. [[1,1],[p,1]]^2 has diagonal 1+p over Z/p^2), whereas the mod-p reading gives the Sylow p-subgroup of GL_n(Z/p^m) studied in the cited Merzlyakov/Kolesnikov papers. Every matrix satisfying the congruences is invertible (det ≡ 1 mod p), so realising P_n as a subgroup of GL loses nothing (c03 even proves this in Lean).

All eight candidates compiled and all stated both slots essentially equivalently; differences were in quality. c01/c05/c08 (direct carrier) and c03 (comap+copy) make membership definitionally the source's condition; c02/c04/c06/c07 wrap the set in Subgroup.closure (mathematically equal since the set is already a subgroup, but indirect), and c06/c07 additionally make the definition of P depend on a proof term hm. c04's regularity uses a single p-th power z^p rather than an element of ℧₁(⟨x,y⟩'); this is equivalent for finite p-groups only via a nontrivial theorem of Hall, so I preferred the closure/product form used by the others. Including IsPGroup in the regularity predicate (c03/c05/c07/c08) adds only the claim 'P_n is a p-group', which the source itself states. Kolesnikov 'for any m' is read as any positive integer m, consistent with the problem's setup.

Dropped items (the main question and the m = 1, m = 2 remarks) were correctly not formalized by any candidate; c05 noted the main question could be stated with answer(sorry), but the decomposition table excludes it.

Final file = c08 with docstring enrichments only; compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
